Leider nicht direkt meines. Die "Dollars"-Trilogie steht schon seit Anbeginn der Zeit auf meiner Watchlist und irgendwie habe ich mich immer etwas davor gesträubt. Vermutlich aufgrund der Tatsache, dass das alles Western sind. Denn mit diesem Genre konnte ich noch nie viel anfangen, hatte allerdings auch die Hoffnung, von eines Besseren belehrt zu werden. Leider war das nicht direkt der Fall. Was ich aber sagen muss ist, dass "A Fistful of Dollars" Momente hatte. Es gab hier und da Szenen, die selbst mich gepackt haben, die actionreich und einfach spaßig waren. Das Problem war vermutlich nur, dass ich nicht vollkommen in der Richtigen Stimmung war. Ich habe mir allerdings ein Szenario ausgemalt, in dem diese Filme besser funktionieren können und ich werde es definitiv erneut probieren, wenn dies der Fall ist. Besonders eben, da ich gesehen habe, dass der Film Momente hat, die eben nicht vollkommen funktioniert haben, auch wenn ich mir das gewünscht hätte. Was aber definitiv sehr stark war, war der Score, der für mich fast den ganzen Film getragen hat. Was Ennio Morricone hier abgeliefert hat, war großartig und hat den Film für mich definitiv aufgewertet. Das Problem ist nur, dass ich die Handlung abgesehen davon leider extrem langweilig fand. Ich kann selbst nicht sagen, woran genau das lag, aber irgendwie kam es mir so vor, als würde nichts passieren. Wie gesagt: hier und da gab es Momente, aber diese waren mir dann doch nicht auf dem Niveau, dass sie noch wirklich viel retten konnte. Sie haben den Film noch okay gemacht, aber für mehr hat es leider nicht gereicht. 2,5/5 Sternen.

Clint Eastwood is the saving grace, and maybe some western tropes were innovated here I am not sure. But overall the plot is haphazard and hard to connect with and close ups provide a lot of filler with little varied emotion.

Clint Eastwood da una parte, Ennio Morricone dall'altra...e Sergio Leone nel mezzo. Con questa pellicola il regista italiano definisce il genere spaghetti western e affina la propria regia con i caratteristici primissimi piani ai volti degli attori. Le ambientazioni, le musiche, i dialoghi indimenticabili e la geniale caratterizzazione dell 'uomo senza nome fanno il resto. Un film fondamentale.

No soc la mes aficionada als westerns, però estic contenta d’haver entès bastant bé l’argument. Clint Eastwood espectacular i preciós. M’ha agradat que es deia alguna frase i més endavant se’n tornava a fer referència. A riffle doesn’t always kill a man with a 45🤗

Westerns aren't like my absolute favorite genre movies, but I do like to see them every once in a while. This one I saw because I've seen The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly once before I knew it was the last of a trilogy. So I wanted to correct that and see the whole thing. I also wanted to see what kind of cinematography they accomplished. This doesn't fit anywhere else, so it's going here: I hate (/sarcastic) how catchy the main theme is. I thought the day-for-night was good, but still made me laugh. I can never take that seriously. The huge barrel rolling down the ramp onto the two guys was a surprisingly good scene within the escape sequence. And there was a good (and sparing) use of dolly shots. I'm ready for the next one.
Chepa frère c’est le premier film de ce bon vieux Sergio que je regarde et c’est peut être pas avec celui là que j’aurais du commencer. (Il n’empêche qu’on va se finir le mois avec sa filmo)

I've got to say Sergio Leone did not do a great job directing this film, and that's reasonable since he evolved and made "The Good, The Bad, The Ugly" afterwards which is an all time masterpiece. Anyways, this movie for me is a classic good concept good ideas bad execution. For some reason the shots were all closeups and extremely bland, and he didn't really do his best setting up the three acts and generally how the movie progresses. But yes for its time it was good, and i guess overall the movie was enjoyable, the third act was really solid, ending's nice.

I'm starting to see a pattern with Leone. The visual language of this film is very strong, it has clearly left its imprint on cinema for decades, the close-up face shots, the way of filming shootouts, the boots, the desert. It's all very pretty, like super pretty, makes me want to go to the USA desert as someone who vehemently hates the States. BUT, there is always a "but" with Leone. The writing is not that good, it's pretty mediocre if you ask me. So many of the plots our protagonists embark on are convoluted as hell and necessitate uber-dumb secondary characters. It's comical. Sorry, my suspension of disbelief isn't that strong. Homeboy has more stealth than prime Batman, but Western fans want to convince me that the superhero genre and the Western don't share many qualities. Sorry to break it to you, but the Western is the superhero movie of the '60s. The aura farming, the duels, the untouchable protagonist, the cool violence trope, the singular man against the force of evil and corruption. I could go on and on. Anyways back to Leone, this is his first movie and you know what, it's fine. Maybe I'm being kind because I know he makes a really great Western in Once Upon a Time in the West and flips many of the tropes that I found frustrating in this one. BUT, there is always a "but" with Leone, his writing of female characters... yikes, this one is bad. And don't give me the "it was the '60s" BS. Also, another thing that I've started to notice in some Leone movies, this one and America , is that he might not condone the usage of violence, and maybe he implies that it's bad, but he never condemns his characters. There is a nuance here. I'll finish the trilogy, I promise, I know you're reading ;) Did the guy from the bar/barn get his money back haha? 6.0/10 When I watch these types of movies and see the way these men act and sometimes the convoluted morality the filmmaker wants to get at, looking at you Nolan,  all my mental roads lead back to Vinland Saga . That story got it right, so it is possible, it just takes time and better writing.

Three stars sounds harsher than it is, i liked it more than i disliked it. I mean it's a spaghetti western with clint eastwood so obviously it was enjoyable. It was great to me that it wasn't another lame story with a cowboy fighting to get the girl in the end, he was just killing people to get rich while saving this girl as a byproduct. Not much to say about this one as it's not quite as serious/heavy as something like The Good, the Bad and the Ugly but still very fun to watch. Low impact on the soul but it's clint eastwood shenanigans so I will prob watch again.

I still think this film is just alright at best.  Definitely the worst out of the Dollars Trilogy.  It has a fairly slow plot, and I’m just not the biggest fan of it.

The dubbing is also really funny as NOTHING lines up lol. the soundtrack however 10/10. an entertaining western, ticking most western stereotypes: Guns ✅ Gringos ✅ Gold ✅ Girls ✅ Gmexicans ✅ a town too small for two people/parties ✅

My least favorite of the three but still a master class in western movies. The story is a little boring and I find that it hasn’t fully embraced the man with no name feeling yet. But it’s still good and there are glimpses.

Problematic fave lol - as a mixed race Indigenous Mexican I surprisingly have a special place in my heart for Westerns. It’s how my Dad learned English as a kid after moving to the US from a ranch in Durango, Mexico. I grew up watching a lot of Westerns with him as a kid and I just loved the energy of being just a wandering bad ass that smokes, fights and solves shit like a boss. It’s a macho masculine main character energy I’m into that’s therapeutic at times. My dad did make sure to constantly say “it wasn’t really like this” and “for natives it’s was actually….” So I grew up knowing that cowboy westerns were like comic book movies in that way. Love the soundtrack to this and the sets. So many bad Mexican accents. Love Clint Eastwood’s facial expressions and ominous line deliveries. This may have been how I learned to threaten people. Maybe Westerns even made me gay 😂☠️

I watched The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly, first. There isn't even a comparison, here. The thing is, A Fistful of dollars plays more like a traditional western, I'd say. Sergio Leone gets a little more satirical with it, with each film, Im  guessing/assuming. I have not seen For A Few Dollars More, yet. However, The Good, the bad and the Ugly is where he really went in with the close ups, and the use of the score. This first film, it course, was the building blocks for that. He walked with this film, so the third one could run. That being said, the whole climax of this film is badass.

Maybe a palette cleanser is needed, but the long drawn aura farming everyone does here didn't resonate. Shit just felt long. Viewing experience was a 32" TV 12+ feet away on low volume. Certainly didn't do Clint any favors with this setup. I'll come back to this one again sometime, slow burn.

J’ai bien été diverti! La musique est extraordinaire vraiment Enio jtm et le film est très bien rythmé. Problème qui m’empêche de mettre une meilleure note, je sais pas pq mon cerveau n’arrivait PAS à ce concentrer tout le long du film. J’ai compris les enjeux principaux avec notre Clint Eastwood qui intervient dans un conflit entre deux clans qui se battent pour…… jle dirai pas 😜, mais vraiment mon cerveau était éteint pendant 1h30 et j’arrivais pas à suivre le cours des événements (ça ne m’a pas empêché de passer un agréable moment nevertheless!). La fin est super tuff et la mentalité de Joe vis à vis de l’Etat en opposition à celle qu’il a envers les gangs est cool. Aussi, je sais pas c’est quoi le problème de France TV mais WHAT THE FUCK les sous titres français genre, à de nombreuses reprises les sous titres ont rien à voir avec les dialogues et des fois y’en a qui apparaissent de nul part ; c’est sûrement basé sur la VF de l’époque mais j’ai eu la flemme de vérifier. En tout cas jvais m’empresser d’aller mater Yojimbo histoire de voir l’original et d’aller avec la rétrospective Kurosawa en salle actuellement, et j’ai hâte d’enchaîner avec la suite de la trilogie 🤠

can we give a big hand to barrels which make a few notable appearances in the third act awesome music throughout the whole film, obviously the whistling is iconic but it surprised me that it didnt feel gimmicky and was woven in neatly enough to become a core part of the films identity. eastwood's voice is similarly noteworthy in this and his whole performance makes the stranger feel so calculated and deliberate. his dubious morality is also an interesting through line. plot was a little half baked personally, although not so much as to make the film unenjoyable, just somewhat plainer than i expected? not much focus is given to the two groups, especially given that they are in contest but one seems much more amoral than the other. well shot enough to make up for it though in my opinion, as the viewing is still good fun!
